pages.text: The Mutating Sprig is hedgecraft made deliberate. Where $(item)Mutandis$() and $(item)Mutandis Extremis$() scatter possibilities, the sprig forces only a few old changes with a steadier hand. It is a tool, not a powder, and each successful working wears it down.

pages.title: Brewing the Sprig
pages.text: Use the older cauldron path. Fill and heat a $(item)Witch's Cauldron$(), keep an altar nearby, drop in an $(item)Ent Twig$() and a $(item)Nether Wart$(), then use $(item)Mutandis Extremis$() on the cauldron.$(br2)The powder is spent, the altar pays the price, and a fresh sprig condenses from the bowl.

pages.title: Practical Mutations
pages.text: Rewoven now restores the core block workings: $(li)$(item)Grass Block$() becomes $(item)Mycelium$()$(li)$(item)Mycelium$() becomes $(item)Grass Block$()$(li)Underwater $(item)Dirt$() becomes $(item)Clay$()$(li)Underwater $(item)Clay$() becomes $(item)Dirt$()$(br2)The first plant-construction mutation is back too: use the sprig on an $(item)empty Chest$() sitting over a water source with $(item)Short Grass$() on each of its four sides, and those grasses will twist into four $(item)Grasspers$().

pages.title: Leech Chest
pages.text: The next old structure route is back as well. Set an $(item)empty Trapped Chest$() in place, put a $(item)Vine$() on each of its four sides, and make sure there is water below each vine. Use the sprig on the trapped chest and it will turn into a $(item)Leech Chest$().$(br2)That matters because the Leech Chest is one of the cleanest repeatable ways to gather stored taglocks in a settlement.

pages.title: Blood Roses
pages.text: Once you have a $(item)Leech Chest$(), set it over a water source and place a $(item)Poppy$() on each of its four sides. Use the sprig on the Leech Chest and the chest will be consumed, leaving four $(item)Blood Roses$().$(br2)Those roses then keep fresh taglock samples until you draw them out with a $(item)Taglock Kit$().

pages.title: Wild Bramble
pages.text: For the old thorn hedge, place a $(item)Cactus$() on $(item)Sand$(), keep water on its four sides, and hang $(item)Spanish Moss$() above each water source. Set $(item)Grasspers$() on the four diagonal corners, feed two with $(item)Bone Meal$() and two with $(item)Blaze Powder$(), then touch the cactus with the sprig.$(br2)The moss and offerings are spent, and the cactus column becomes $(item)Wild Bramble$().

pages.title: Void Bramble
pages.text: The stranger sister begins the same way, but with $(item)Sugar Cane$() in the center. Water still rings the stalk, $(item)Spanish Moss$() still hangs over each source, and the four diagonal $(item)Grasspers$() must each hold an $(item)Ender Pearl$().$(br2)Use the sprig on the cane and the whole stalk twists into $(item)Void Bramble$(), which answers the old Ender Bramble role by throwing intruders elsewhere.

pages.title: Wormwood
pages.text: The old conjurer's herb is also back on the sprig. Raise a fully grown $(item)Wheat$() plant, keep the four diagonal corners watered one block down, and plant $(item)Wispy Cotton$() on each cardinal side. Use the sprig on the ripe wheat and the cotton will be consumed, leaving a fresh young $(item)Wormwood$() in its place.$(br2)That gives the Brazier's necromantic smoke a proper survival bridge again.
